title: fleet never walks into a directory named _Archive
body:
## What happened

hv has ruled, more than once and again on 2026-11-13 in devbin-vc's window ("Nothing in _Archive. It's an ARCHIVE."; "I HAVE TOLD YOU MULTIPLE TIMES THAT WE IGNORE _ARCHIVE"), that archives are never swept. `fleet upgrade`, `fleet audit` and `fleet doc` walk every directory under `fleet.roots`, and `~/Devel/prj/_Archive` sits under the `~/Devel/prj` root. So the 0.1.23 sweep upgraded `_Archive/Intentv2` (its commit c9477cdf, in that tree's own repository). Today only a `DEVBIN_FLEET_FROZEN` set by hand keeps it out, which an operator can forget, as vc did.

## The ask

The census skips any path component named `_Archive`, at any depth, by rule rather than by a frozen list. Following the existing EXCLUSIONS ARE REPORTED rule (bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:496), it names each skipped tree once, as "ARCHIVE -- not walked". It needs a test arm with an estate under `_Archive`.

## Why it matters

A sweep that reaches an archive writes into a tree hv has said is never touched, and the frozen list that prevents it today depends on the operator remembering it on every run.

## Resolution

Fixed in one landing on main, 68c316551d4542a7fbb1d1cadd83cd3c2f113626 (2026-11-13 09:33Z), unit 0351-1 from the tested tip f23e8069, in devbin 0.1.24's batch; unpushed until devbin's next cut. It was proved on its own arms under hv's rule of 2026-11-05 (red at the base's code, green at the fix) on devbin-vc's desk.

- The census prunes any directory named `_Archive`, at any depth, by rule. bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet marks it in the walk's own prune group, beside a vendored lib, so it is never entered and nothing in it is read, and DEVBIN_FLEET_FROZEN is no longer needed to keep one out.
- Each one is named once, following EXCLUSIONS ARE REPORTED:
  - kind_of answers `archive` by the name alone;
  - audit gives it a row whose every cell but kind and path reads `not walked`;
  - upgrade's not-swept table names it `ARCHIVE -- not walked`, and its summary line counts it;
  - the document gives archives a section of their own when there is one.
- The walk outside the roots prunes archives by name too, and every report's "not walked" line says so.
- fleet's help page carries the rule.

Five new arms in fleet.bats build archives under the test's own roots and home only, never a real `_Archive`, at one depth and at two, with an estate in each: audit, the sweep (its --apply runs nothing in one and leaves its files as they were), the document with an archive and without one, and the walk outside the roots. Four were red at the base, each on its own finding, and the fifth (the document with no archive) is green there by construction. fleet.bats was green whole at the fix, under BSD and GNU. 0.1.24's note carries it under Fixed, devbin's own tree.
